0,3,1: Week 3 - Getting in before the tender
0,4,1:
George Berrington (BeDeveloped)
Andrew Fenwick (Managing Director)
Kate Rowley (Sales Director)
1,0,1: George Berrington led a demand generation session with Andrew Fenwick and Kate Rowley focused on reaching buyers before tenders are published. Elmstead currently has no outbound activity and relies on tender portals. We agreed a partner-led outbound programme into named change directors and a small roundtable series, with tender portal monitoring kept but deprioritised.
5,1,1: Sharpen discovery and qualification so partners turn pre-tender conversations into shaped opportunities.
5,2,1: Kate to bring the current bid/no-bid checklist and two recent proposals.
2,1,1: Kate confirmed almost all opportunities come from tender portal alerts and two frameworks. There is no outbound and the website gets about 300 visits a month.
2,2,1: Andrew noted that many public bodies run pre-market engagement events six to nine months before a tender. Elmstead rarely attends them. George suggested treating these as a primary channel.
2,3,1: Kate worried partners will not find time for outbound. Andrew agreed to ring-fence half a day a week for each of the five partners.
3,1,1: Shift effort to 50 percent outbound and pre-market engagement, 30 percent frameworks and 20 percent open tenders over the next two quarters.
3,2,1: Each of the five partners to run a named list of 25 change directors, with half a day a week ring-fenced for outreach.
3,4,1: Run a quarterly roundtable in Leeds for water utility change directors, capped at 12 attendees.
3,5,1: Use a six-touch sequence over 30 days mixing LinkedIn, email and a phone call from the partner.
3,7,1: Track pre-tender conversations as the lead metric, targeting 20 per quarter, rather than tender alerts received.
4,1,0: Build partner target lists of 25 change directors each
4,2,0: Book every pre-market engagement event in the water and NHS calendars for the next six months
